text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition alone proves nothing. All-female panels occur by chance regularly, especially on small committees, and raising it as your main point will read as an accusation you can't support — which tends to destroy your credibility on the stronger parts of your case.

Your stronger ground is substantive: a completed PhD and six papers versus an unfinished PhD and two, plus the unanswered request for written reasons. Most public universities owe you that explanation within a set period. Chase it formally, in writing, citing the relevant regulation or your union.

Then judge. If the reasons genuinely weight industry experience and that was in the advertisement, it's likely legitimate. If they're vague or shift, escalate — on the merits, not the panel's sex.
